To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with a history of periodontitis have a higher risk for peri-implant diseases, peri-implants failures, and post-operative infections than healthy periodontal patients.
the risk of post-operative infections is increased by a factor of 2.3, peri-implants disease by a factor of three, implant failures by a factor of four and marginal bone loss by a factor of two.

periodontally compromised patients with a high level of plaque control are at higher risk for post-operative infections, marginal bone loss around implants (peri-implantic diseases) and implant failures compared with periodontally healthy individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether periodontally compromised patients have an increased risk of post-operative infections and implant failures in the context of implant therapy.
the effect of the periodontal status of the patient on implant survival and peri-implant health.
the risk factors associated with dental implant failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of implant placement in patients with increased periodontal susceptibility is higher compared to periodontally-healthy patients.
the implant survival rate is higher in periodontally healthy than in patients with a history of periodontitis.

the risk of implant failures in periodontally compromised patients is higher compared to periodontally sound patients, but this risk can be minimized by careful preoperative planning and meticulous post-operative maintenance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with increased susceptibility for periodontitis are at higher risk of post-operative complications, peri-implanat diseases and implant failures.
the implant survival rates are lower in periodontally compromised patients than healthy patients.
patients who have been treated for periodontitis are at higher risk for post-operative infection and peri-implant diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of implant failures is increased in periodontally compromised patients, however, the magnitude of the increase is unknown and needs to be further evaluated.
periodontally compromised patients may not be suitable for implant placement.
periodontally compromised patients should be treated with caution when implant placement is considered.
